title: 〜には及ばない
meaning: there is no need to …; cannot match …
simpleExplanation: 及ぶ means "to reach". 〜には及ばない has two uses. (1) Polite refusal of trouble: "there is no need to X" (ご心配には及びません = please don't worry). (2) Comparison: "cannot reach the level of X" (彼女には及ばない = I'm no match for her). Sense 1 is about actions; sense 2 is about ability.
whenUsed: Sense 1 is polite formal speech: telling a customer or superior that they need not go to the trouble (お礼・心配・お越しいただく). Sense 2 appears in both speech and writing, often with 到底 or とても for emphasis, and expresses modesty or admiration.
formation: Vる + には及ばない (行く・心配する・驚く)
ご/お + N + には及びません (ご心配・お礼・ご足労)
N(person/thing) + には(到底)及ばない = cannot match

diagram.title: Two senses of には及ばない

examples.ja: わざわざお越しいただくには及びません。
examples.reading: わざわざおこしいただくにはおよびません。
examples.en: There is no need for you to go to the trouble of coming.
examples.note: Sense 1: polite refusal of the trouble of coming. わざわざ often appears.

examples.ja: ご心配には及びません。すぐに回復します。
examples.reading: ごしんぱいにはおよびません。すぐにかいふくします。
examples.en: There is no need to worry. I will recover soon.
examples.note: ご心配には及びません is a set phrase reassuring someone.

examples.ja: 英語の発音では、彼女には到底及ばない。
examples.reading: えいごのはつおんでは、かのじょにはとうていおよばない。
examples.en: In English pronunciation, I cannot come close to her.
examples.note: Sense 2: cannot reach her level. 到底 strengthens it.

examples.ja: その程度のことで驚くには及ばない。
examples.reading: そのていどのことでおどろくにはおよばない。
examples.en: There is no need to be surprised at something like that.
examples.note: Sense 1 with a verb of reaction (驚く・慌てる).

examples.ja: 私の腕前では、プロには到底及ばない。
examples.reading: わたしのうでまえでは、プロにはとうていおよばない。
examples.en: With my skill, I cannot come close to a professional.

similarGrammar.difference: "No need to" because the matter is trivial or obvious. までもない is neutral; には及ばない is more polite and often addressed to the listener.
"No need to (be surprised / praise)" because the reaction is not warranted. Judges appropriateness rather than politely declining.
Everyday "there is no need to" (心配することはない). Same meaning as sense 1, plainer register.

commonMistakes.right: ご心配には及びません。
commonMistakes.why: The set phrase includes は: には及ばない.

commonMistakes.wrong: 彼は私には及ばない。（意味：私は彼にかなわない）
commonMistakes.why: X は Y には及ばない means X falls short of Y. Keep the order straight: the weaker one is the subject.

commonMistakes.wrong: 手伝うには及びませんか。
commonMistakes.why: には及ばない is what the receiver says to decline; do not use it to offer help.

usageNotes: Sense 1 is a courteous way to say "don't bother" to someone of higher status; it does not sound cold.
Sense 2 often takes 到底・とても・遠く for emphasis: 遠く及ばない = nowhere near.
The affirmative 及ぶ is used in the pattern 〜に及ぶ (extend to), which is a different grammar.
jlptTips: ご心配 / お礼 / わざわざ + blank at the end of a polite reply: には及びません.
Distractors: までもない, に当たらない, ことはない. If the sentence is a polite reply to an offer, choose には及ばない.
For the comparison sense, look for 到底 or a skill noun (腕前・英語力) before the blank.
